review.alternative: Full microscopic trajectories might yield exact entropy production if spatial-temporal resolution is complete.
review.would_change_mind: Direct measurement of exact microscopic trajectories without coarse-graining information loss.

claims.statement: Coarse-graining of underlying Markovian dynamics restricts entropy production retrieval to lower bounds.

support.explanation: Demonstrates that coarse-graining limits entropy production retrieval to lower bounds.
support.passage: For many systems, the full information of an underlying Markovian decription is not accessible due to limited spatial or temporal resolution. We first show that such an often inevitable coarse-graining implies that, rather than the full entropy production, only a lower bound can be retrieved from coarse-grained data.

actions.findings: Coarse-graining of underlying Markovian dynamics restricts entropy production retrieval to lower bounds. [peer-0916f25fdd8ff50318f79967]
actions.limitations: Models remain constrained by the absence of fully resolved non-Markovian microscopic trajectories.
actions.next_questions: How do specific error-correction overheads alter the lower bounds of thermodynamic dissipation in physical memories?
actions.reason: Revising the notebook to integrate new evidence on coarse-grained entropy production and channel memory.
actions.summary: Energy costs and retention times in physical memories are fundamentally bounded by coarse-graining and non-equilibrium dissipation constraints.
actions.title: Thermodynamic Costs of Memory Reliability (Revised)
